Required course assignments do not bypass approval and separate course-linked exams retain their own policies. Audit events capture before/after state atomically. features.feature: Live exam monitoring, saved-answer inspection and time grants
verification: frontend/e2e/training.spec.ts::individual attempt limits, live monitoring and safe time extensions
features.assessment: Managers monitor account/guest attempts with saved-answer counts, heartbeat/save times, scoped filters and pagination; private previews are excluded. Individual saved answers and frozen questions can be inspected read-only without changing participant contact times. Audited active extensions and explicit completed-paper reopening use bounded time grants and durable client request IDs to recover lost responses once. Reopening preserves the previous answers, questions, grades, feedback and submitted time in protected, manager-only paginated history; it withdraws the current result and requires fresh review after resubmission. Only the latest submission can reopen, with exam-first locking against concurrent starts. The same identity, attempt number, frozen policy and budgets are retained; guest access and invitation validity remain enforced. Revision checks reject stale learner writes and review forms. Learner timers retain local edits and synchronize server deadlines. PostgreSQL tests cover simultaneous grants, reopen/start/review races and expiry lock waits; browser acceptance covers saved-answer inspection, lost-response reopening recovery, guest resume, regrading, preserved evidence, mobile layout and three languages.

Validation covers bounds, finite decimal marks, duplicate rows, malformed CSV, stale papers, scope and size limits. Feedback-only edits retain pending essay grading or automatic scoring; clearing comments is explicit. Bounded batches apply atomically with unchanged answers, submission times and quotas; reports and completion use the same overridden score calculation. Durable protected receipts retain reasons, before/after question marks/comments and result predictions. Lost apply responses recover by the saved import ID without a second write. Reopening/review/import concurrency, expiry after lock waits, rollback, retention and stale forms are tested on PostgreSQL; browser acceptance covers account/guest results, multilingual/mobile preview, response loss and later grading without rewriting original receipts.

remediations: Scormly company publication now offers SCORM 1.2 and 2004. Both versions have real browser coverage from demo-project publication through source ZIP download, isolated playback, durable bookmark saving and resumed playback.

The publication picker filters courses by server-provided management rights and explains when no eligible course exists. Browser coverage verifies a visible read-only course cannot be selected; upload permissions remain server-enforced.
SCORM imports now recognize CAM 1.3 declarations as 2004, including case/whitespace variants. Regression tests use actual manifest ZIPs.

SCORM launch context now supplies current learner ID/name, safely escapes embedded JSON and rejects deactivated accounts. Regression coverage includes name fallbacks and overriding stale saved identity.
English, Traditional Chinese and Spanish include the new publication controls. The studio build and 197 unit tests pass (4 upstream skips); complete per-block acceptance is still pending.

Integer, numeric-with-tolerance and ordering questions now work through bank and exam authoring, frozen attempts, autosave/resume, automatic grading, guest limits, learner/instructor review and assessment insights. English, Traditional Chinese and Spanish have browser coverage, including keyboard ordering and mobile layout.

Yaksh draft import now preserves alternative integer values and individual floating error margins. Arrange import requires an explicitly reviewed correct_order because the native export omits reliable testcase ordering metadata. Invalid imports remain atomic.

Retry intervals now share one server-enforced clock across account aliases and guest links. Eligibility is measured from the previous start, active attempts resume, early starts do not consume budgets, and account/assignment/guest interfaces show localized availability. PostgreSQL concurrency and real browser workflows cover the new policy.

Yaksh string matching now preserves each accepted answer’s case and spacing policy, including multiline and Unicode distinctions. Three-language bank/exam authoring, frozen attempts, account/guest grading, labeled reviews, rule-aware analytics and atomic string imports share these rules. Historical normalized grading remains compatible.

Sequential exam navigation is now enforced in the API, including private future questions, persisted unlocking, incomplete-submission validation and frozen attempt rules. Completed response visibility remains a live organizer setting with no-store responses, scoped instructor access and participant refresh. Account/guest and PostgreSQL concurrency coverage preserve existing budgets, autosave and timeout behavior.

The active exam player now uses monotonic elapsed time for deadlines and save-retry delays, anchored to server timestamps. Changing the device wall clock cannot prematurely submit an exam or reset its duration; server-side expiry remains authoritative.

Instructor exam previews now provide a complete saved question-paper view, timed learner simulation and untimed draft testing. Trials use a separate private model, shared production question/grading rules, resumable autosaves, independent test grading and bounded retention. Tests verify that successful trials cannot change existing participant evidence or assignment completion.

Y43 now includes read-only active-answer inspection and explicit, audited reopening of the latest submission, with immutable prior evidence, unchanged attempt budgets, stale-write protection and retry recovery. Account/guest access, PostgreSQL reopening/start/review races and the three-language browser workflow are covered. This completes the monitoring/time-grant feature group; other assessment and course gaps remain.

Y45 now provides native marks CSV template, validation, review, atomic application and durable receipts for account/guest exams. All seven question types support imported points/comments, with fresh grading revisions, scoped access, unchanged quotas and PostgreSQL concurrency coverage. The original Yaksh wide CSV schema requires conversion to the new exact-attempt template.

Y07 now provides opt-in course enrollment requests and scoped review queues, rejection/reapplication, removal/restoration, audit history and stale-decision protection. Course lessons and isolated SCORM content enforce current admission while preserving prior learning evidence. PostgreSQL concurrency, multilingual forms, mobile layout and lost-review-response recovery have acceptance coverage.

validation.result: 202 tests passed on PostgreSQL 17, including 12 admission tests covering content privacy, request/review transitions, preserved completion/bookmarks, scoped access/CSRF, policy changes, required assignments, pagination, localization, audit rollback, lost responses and concurrent request/review/removal/completion. Existing assessment, grading, monitoring, identity, reporting and SCORM regressions remain green.

All 20 browser workflows passed together against the real PostgreSQL-backed API and isolated content server with file-mail configured. Course admission coverage creates an approval-required lesson, checks hidden content, rejects and reapplies, recovers a committed review after response loss, preserves form edits in three languages, checks mobile overflow, completes learning and removes/restores access without losing completion evidence. Existing marks-import and private-preview checks also pass after fixing late review GET responses that could overwrite newly typed grades in development StrictMode.
Both passed. Existing JavaScript chunk-size advisories remain.
